insights.headline: Meta Connect 2026: new glasses, a lighter headset, and AI that shops for you
insights.label: Meta Connect
key_facts: Meta VR Glasses is a tethered headset priced at $1,299.99, releasing next spring
Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 glasses start at $449 in the US, $70 more than the predecessor's original launch price
Meta's supported smart glasses are now FDA-certified hearing aids for mild to moderate hearing loss, unlocked with a one-time $149 purchase
Meta held its Connect 2026 keynote at company headquarters in Menlo Park, California
Ray-Ban Meta Audio glasses are available for pre-order at $349 and ship October 13
Meta is integrating Muse AI shopping with retailers including Walmart, Best Buy, American Eagle Outfitters, DICK'S Sporting Goods and Instacart for making purchases on your behalf
Meta VR Glasses weighs about 100 grams, roughly one-fifth the weight of Quest 3 glasses
Meta VR Glasses runs on Qualcomm's Snapdragon Reality Elite chip via a tethered puck offering up to three hours of continuous high-resolution media playback and 45W fast charging
Meta VR Glasses will have 75 games playable at launch using hand gestures, with support for Quest games via Touch Plus controllers and Xbox Cloud Gaming
Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 features a single 12MP camera, 3K Ultra HD video, a six-microphone array, and up to nine hours of battery life
Ray-Ban Meta Audio, Meta's first camera-free glasses, weigh 43g and come in 23 frame and lens combinations
Meta VR Glasses is the first VR device to receive IMAX Enhanced certification and supports Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos
insights.what_changed: Meta held Connect 2026 on Sept 23, unveiling four new devices (Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3, Ray-Ban Meta Audio, Meta VR Glasses, Muse Charm), new AI shopping integrations via Muse with Walmart/Instacart, FDA-certified hearing aid functionality for smart glasses, a 'hologram' video call feature, and a Quest/VR gaming ecosystem update including Beat Saber's biggest overhaul.
